module_title: Models of Blended Learning & Inverting Bloom's Taxonomy
introduction: This intermediate tier drives into the specific structural models of Blended Learning (Rotation, Flex, A La Carte) and explains the profound connection between the Flipped Classroom and Bloom's Taxonomy.

core_concepts.title: The Flipped Classroom and Bloom's Taxonomy
core_concepts.description:
The pedagogical genius of the Flipped Classroom lies in how it maps to Bloom's Taxonomy of Cognitive Domains.
- Lower Order Thinking Skills (LOTS): Remembering and Understanding. In a flipped model, students do this easily AT HOME by watching a video. They don't need a teacher just to listen to facts.
- Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS): Applying, Analyzing, Evaluating, and Creating. In a flipped model, students do this IN CLASS. This is the hardest part of learning, and they now have the teacher physically present to guide them through complex analysis and creation.

core_concepts.title: The 4 Core Models of Blended Learning
core_concepts.description:
1. Rotation Model: Students rotate on a fixed schedule between different learning stations, at least one of which is online. 
   - Subtypes include: Station Rotation (within one classroom), Lab Rotation (moving to a computer lab), and Flipped Classroom (rotating between home and school).
2. Flex Model: The backbone of learning is online. Students move on fluid, individually customized schedules. The teacher is present to provide on-demand tutoring or small-group help.
3. A La Carte Model: Students take a traditional face-to-face course at school, but intentionally take one or more courses completely online (e.g., an Advanced Physics course not offered at their local school).
4. Enriched Virtual Model: The student completes the vast majority of coursework online at home, but is required to attend school for mandatory face-to-face enrichment sessions (unlike purely online schools).

core_concepts.title: Benefits and Challenges
core_concepts.description:
- Benefits: Personalized pacing (students can rewind the lecture video 10 times if they don't understand), immediate feedback during class, and high engagement.
- Challenges: The 'Digital Divide' (students without internet access cannot watch the home lecture), lack of self-discipline among younger students to watch the video at home.

important_entities.name: Station Rotation
important_entities.key_fact: The most common Blended model in Primary Schools.
important_entities.description: In a 45-minute class, the teacher divides students into 3 groups. Group 1 works with the teacher on reading. Group 2 works independently on a worksheet. Group 3 works on tablets using a math app. Every 15 minutes, the groups rotate. This ensures small-group teacher attention and integrated digital learning.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a teacher says 'Watch this YouTube video and email me your doubts,' it is **Asynchronous**. If the teacher says 'Log into Microsoft Teams at 10:00 AM for our live discussion,' it is **Synchronous**. Exams frequently mix these up in scenario-based questions.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: LOTS at Home, HOTS in Class
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Lower-Order Thinking Skills (LOTS) = Home. Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) = Class.

exam_strategy_tips: If a UGC NET question asks 'In which blended model is the curriculum primarily delivered online but students must still attend a brick-and-mortar campus for tutoring?', select the **Flex Model**.
